evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Rafael M. Batista and Thomas L. Griffiths
evidence_items.locator: Discussion, paragraph comparing Default GPT and Rule Confirming; supporting statistics in Results, Discovery Rates
evidence_items.explanation: Default feedback resembled explicitly confirming feedback; discovery was 5.9% with default feedback versus 29.5% with independent samples, an exploratory difference with p<.001. However, the confirming-versus-disconfirming comparison was not significant (p=.143), limiting the strength of that particular contrast.

The prospective protocol specifies randomized feedback conditions and an objective rule-discovery outcome. No data had been collected at registration; the completed paper was public in February, establishing 2026 as the experiment year.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; John Conlon and Peter Schwardmann
evidence_items.locator: Abstract; experiment dates verified in CESifo version, section 2.8
evidence_items.explanation: This experiment found that measurably sycophantic advice could still move choices away from initial leanings overall. It limits generalization but does not refute an impairment that can occur under confirmation-selecting feedback.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence does not establish effects on creative quality or real scientific discovery.
The strongest independent-sampling comparison was exploratory; the preregistered confirming-versus-disconfirming discovery comparison was not significant.
The cited experimental report was a preprint; independent replication was not established.
